title: Review of c37's SH fission correction: replicates on fresh seed 6 (ar=0.02): 64 break-ups of molecules with >= 2 spots, 40 with both pieces >= 2 spots, 18 still apart 50 t later; early events tear loose clusters apart during die-back, later ones (t=495-810) chip 3-6-spot pieces off 50-60-spot molecules
summary: Ran the correction's world.py and fission.py unchanged at its setting (N=128, L=80, cr=0.1, ar=0.02, kap 0.3, tau 10, t=1000) on unused seed 6, plus a labkit pack. fission.py: 64 break-ups (parent >= 2 spots), 40 with both pieces >= 2 spots, 18 of 40 checkable ones persistent (pieces in different molecules 50 t later; fission_ar02_seed6.txt). Listed persistent events: 9 at t=170-375 (21 -> 20 + 4, 33 -> 23 + 23 + 3, 25 -> 13 + 12) while the resource is depleted, and 6 at t=495-810 in which a 50-61-spot molecule sheds a 3-6-spot piece (55 -> 34 + 18 is the one balanced late event). fission_events_seed6.png shows loose clusters separating, as c37 describes. With my seed-5 run in 20261026T1007-c39-review-sh-no-fission (36 of 57 persistent) the correction holds on three seeds (c37's 0, my 5 and 6).

observations.D: fission_ar02_seed6.txt: 18 persistent break-ups with both pieces >= 2 spots on seed 6; fission_events_seed6.png

verdicts.limitation: Supports the correction's statement (break-ups exist and are fragmentation, not shown to be reproduction); it does not support D. Late events are mostly small pieces shed by large molecules, closer to budding of debris than to division into similar parts. 'Molecule' depends on the 2.2-unit linking distance. One setting, one seed.
